precepts.text: Teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed. If you are not applying this, sisters, you are blasphemous, and at the judgment seat, but my husband did this, will be answered, that was the man I gave you.
precepts.point: As the sun when it ariseth, so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house. As the clear light upon the holy candlestick, so is the beauty of the face in ripe age: apply this and your husband sees you beautiful past the gray hairs. As gold pillars upon sockets of silver, so are the fair feet with a constant heart. Beauty is functional, not sexualized; order equals beauty. Wives who neglect the home for other things are out of alignment with God's will; the home is the first priority, husband first, then children.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
Sirach praises “A shamefaced and faithful woman”, “the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house”, and “the fair feet with a constant heart.” Beauty is functional, not sexualized. Order equals beauty, sisters. Wives who neglect the home for other things are out of order and out of alignment with God’s will. The home is your first priority above all things, starting with your husband and then your children.

Titus spells out that order: “That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.” Keepers at home is what the ordering of her house goes into. It teaches them to love their husbands, and sums it up: obedient to their own husbands.

“That the word of God be not blasphemed.” If y’all are not applying this, sisters, you are blasphemous. And you think God will look past it, and at the judgment seat you will say, but my husband did this, my husband did that? He will say, that is blasphemy; that was the man I gave you.

If submission depends on how he treats you, it is not submission; it is manipulation. God told you to submit to your husband in everything, with no caveat. Proverbs 31 without genuine submission is decoration on a house with a weak foundation. Be soft, respectful and quiet; it is not your job to fix his issues but to make sure you are right.

This is the biblical model: complementary responsibilities. The woman’s list seems longer, but the man’s carries more weight. He is the head of the wife as Christ is head of the church, the savior of the body, accountable for you, the house, the children and the nation. Your accountability is only for yourself. Does that not deserve honor?

precepts.text: Exhort servants not to purloin but to show all good fidelity.
precepts.point: Onesimus was a servant who fled Philemon, and Paul sent him back as a brother.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again”: not talking back. Esau perverted this. But read on: “Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.” To purloin is to steal something: sticky fingers, a kleptomaniac. That is what was read in Exodus 22. Paul is dealing with brothers who were stealing, got caught, and were sold to make restitution.

Philemon shows it plainly. Paul met Onesimus while under arrest. He had been a servant to Philemon, and he ran away: “For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever; Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved”. Deal with him like a brother beloved.

Was he a servant because he was poor, or because he did something bad? “If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account”. He owed something because he stole or broke something, and Paul said, put it on my account.

So Paul was dealing with servants who were Hebrews, Israelites in servitude to other Israelites. Chattel slavery came later, when Israel fell by the edge of the sword and was led away captive into all nations, under Rome, Spain and Portugal, France, Britain and the United States.

precepts.text: The aged women are to be teachers of good things, that they may teach the young women to love their husbands and children, to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, obedient to their own husbands.
precepts.point: A sister helping to build up other sisters new in the congregation is right, and the sisters bless the nation with real talents, raising the children in the commandments, and the aged women teaching the young women. But teaching and leading the nation is not the place the Most High set for her.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
Leadership of the nation belongs to men, but the sisters bless the nation with real talents, raising the children in the commandments, and the aged women teaching the young women. “The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things.”

What are they teachers of? “That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.”

A sister helping to build up other sisters new in the congregation is right; that is the place the Most High set for her. Teaching and leading the nation is not, which is why Moses asked for a man over the congregation.

precepts.text: The grace of God teaches us to deny ungodliness and worldly lusts and to live soberly and righteously, so grace itself teaches us to keep the commandments.
precepts.point: We get clean by taking heed to the word and the commandments, not by water baptism.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Grace does not do away with the commandments; it teaches them. “For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world”.

The grace of God teaches us to deny ungodliness and worldly lusts and to live soberly and righteously. So grace itself teaches us to keep the commandments. That is how David was upright before the Lord and kept himself from his iniquity, and how we get clean today.

precepts.text: Speak thou the things which become sound doctrine, meaning the laws of the Most High, this Bible spoken in wisdom.
precepts.point: Let those that fear Thee turn unto me, and those that have known Thy testimonies. Let my heart be sound in Thy statutes, that I be not ashamed, sound in the wisdom of this Bible among the nations.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“But speak thou the things which become sound doctrine”. Sound doctrine is the laws of the Most High, this Bible spoken in wisdom.

A heart sound in his statutes speaks the things which become sound doctrine. That is how the servant is not ashamed, and how those that fear the Most High are glad when they see him, because he has hoped in his word.

precepts.point: When it says 'according to the will of God and our Father,' God refers to Christ (who is called God in Hebrews 1:8) and Father refers to the Most High.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Christ gave himself “that he might deliver us from this present evil world”, and grace is how that deliverance works in us. “For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world.”

The grace of God teaches us to deny ungodliness and worldly lust. Grace gives us a chance and opportunity to overcome sins through mercy; if you keep striving and fighting, eventually you will overcome. Grace also teaches us to keep the commandments in this present world.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded. In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity, sound speech that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you. These are the examples of how men are supposed to conduct themselves, with one another and with our wives.

The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, teachers of good things; that they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home.
Keepers at home: she takes care of her house; there is enough pertaining to her own house for her to deal with. She is not idle, she is not a busybody in everybody else's house.

Obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed. The word of God is blasphemed when a wife who claims she believes is not obedient to her husband. What is the difference between a man who does not provide, who the scripture says is worse than an infidel, and a woman who does not submit? She is not a believer. You can tell if a woman believes the Bible by how she deals with her husband: her tone, her reverence, not going back and forth with him, dealing with him like she would deal with the Lord.
So, Israel, we got to play our position as disciplined soldiers, soldiers with a biblical education. We can't get caught up. We cannot get caught up.

Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded: when it say be sober minded, a lot of times we think, okay, yeah, don't smoke weed, don't be drunk. Yeah, absolutely. But it's also going to keep a clear head in all situations. Keep a clear head. Possess your soul.

That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands. Why do the young women need to be taught to love their husbands? Because it is not in them unless you teach them; the older women teach the younger, and it becomes a cycle.

Discussed in class: what was done to us historically; how the home was split, how Esau stepped in and replaced the man in the home, how the crack epidemic took men out of the home and the disdain for the men grew. We are the only nation whose women say we do not need a man while depending on the system. But we are not the same men; we are taking back what belongs to us. And sisters, even where a brother has done wrong: if you love the Lord, you respect him anyway. Your respect is a reflection of your belief and faith in Christ; without it, you are just as bad as him.
